LESSON: READING 2.2.1READING FLUENCY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency, part of Strand 2 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we ensure we read fluently? 2. Why is reading fluently important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read a story with correct intonation for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use correct expression when reading a text for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate reading a variety of texts for fluency.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read a story with correct intonation for effective communication,

   Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use correct expression when reading a text for fluency,

   Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate reading a variety of texts for fluency.

   Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. conduct a reader’s theatre to read a short passage on the theme with correct intonation,

2. watch a video recording illustrating reading with expression in class,

3. role play reading a news bulletin report on the weather forecast creatively and with expression,

4. record the role play using a digital device for peer review,

5. share experiences about reading fluently in small groups. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. conduct a reader’s theatre to read a short passage on the theme with correct intonation,
2. watch a video recording illustrating reading with expression in class,
3. role play reading a news bulletin report on the weather forecast creatively and with expression,
4. record the role play using a digital device for peer review,
5. share experiences about reading fluently in small groups. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 2.2.1Reading Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with technology to record the role-play using a digital device for

peer review.

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: This is developed as the learner explores views when sharing experiences about

reading fluently in small groups

10

Values:
• Responsibility: This is developed as the learner diligently takes up assigned roles during group activities.

• Unity: This is promoted as the learner interacts harmoniously with peers to role-play a news bulletin report on weather.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Education: This is promoted as the learner acquires knowledge on elements of weather and weather patterns.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of weather to their learning of similar concepts in Social Studies.

Main points to remember:

1. read a story with correct intonation for effective communication,
2. use correct expression when reading a text for fluency,
3. appreciate reading a variety of texts for fluency.

Remember the key question: How can we ensure we read fluently? 2. Why is reading fluently important?
